## Physical scenario

In figure, the waves along rays 1 and 2 are initially in phase, with the same wavelength \( \lambda \) in air. Ray 2 goes through a material with length \( L \) and index of refraction \( n \). The rays are then reflected by mirrors to a common point \( P \) on a screen. Suppose that we can vary \( L \) from 0 to 2400\,\text{nm}. Suppose also that, from \( L = 0 \) to \( L_s = 900\,\text{nm} \), the intensity \( I \) of the light at point \( P \) varies with \( L \) as given in figure.

## Question

What multiple of \( \lambda \) gives the phase difference between ray 1 and ray 2 at common point \( P \) when \( L = 1200\,\text{nm} \)?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 0.40λ

- B: B: 1.20λ

- C: C: 0.80λ

- D: D: 1.60λ

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image is a graph depicting a curve on a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled "L (nm)" with values ranging from 0 to \(L_s\). The vertical axis is labeled "I". The curve starts high on the vertical axis at \(L = 0\) and decreases smoothly to a minimum before slightly rising again as it approaches \(L_s\). The curve is thick and smooth, and grid lines are present to aid in reading the graph. No specific numerical values are indicated.
